setup.zh: 褚先生讲灵根：一门者，灵气如江河；五门者，灵气如漏勺。满堂哄笑。「沈小满。你说，漏勺能打水吗？」
setup.en: Master Chu lectures on roots: one door, and the qi comes like a river; five doors, and it runs off like a skimmer. The hall roars. "Shen Xiaoman. Tell me — can a skimmer carry water?"

recap.zh: 褚先生当堂问你：漏勺能打水吗？你说：能，多打几次。
recap.en: Master Chu asked you before the whole hall whether a skimmer can carry water. You said: yes — go back for more.

zh: 褚先生讲灵根，山羊胡子一翘。
en: Master Chu lectures on roots; his goat's beard jerks.
"Five doors — a mixed root: the qi runs off like a skimmer."
"Shen Xiaoman. Tell me — can a skimmer carry water?"

text.zh: 胡子一翘一翘，倒像在替他点头；你暗暗数了，他讲一段，要翘七回。
text.en: The goatee bobs up and down as if nodding for him. You count on the quiet: seven bobs to a passage.

text.zh: 戒尺一头磨得发亮，另一头却新得很——先生打人，只用一头。
text.en: One end of the ruler is worn bright; the other looks new. The master only ever strikes with one end.

story.zh:
新入门的弟子，每日辰时上课。头一天，钟敲过了，讲堂里的新弟子还在交头接耳，忽然有人「咦」了一声，指着窗外。后山半腰的云，叫什么从里头分开了：一道青光斜斜地落下来，不快，像一片叶子顺着风往下飘。近了，才看清是一个人，脚底下踩着一口剑，一身灰袍叫风鼓起来，两只大袖往后飘着，袍角翻卷，颏下一撮胡子也飘着；他身子四周裹着一层淡淡的白气，像山腰上撕下来的一缕云，跟着他走。他从三重屋脊上头掠过去，屋脊上歇着的一排麻雀一只也没惊起。满堂的人都挤到了窗口，后头的踩着凳子，孙二狗踮着脚，下巴搁在小满肩膀上。

青光在讲堂门口一停，散了。他从剑上下来，脚落地，没有一点声音；那身鼓着的袍子，这才慢慢地垂了下来。砖缝里渗出来的那层白气，本来贴着地皮懒懒地流，这时候一齐往他脚边涌过去，绕着他的鞋打了个旋儿，像一群见了主人的狗。他两根手指往回一招，那口剑「铮」地轻吟一声，自己缩回他背后的鞘里；他背着手进了门。满堂一下子没了声。坐在门边的几个，后颈上的汗毛先立了起来，像冬天推门，迎面一股冷气——又不是冷，是满屋的灵气都往他身上去了。不知是谁先站了起来，跟着一屋子人全站了起来，凳子腿刮着砖地，「吱吱嘎嘎」响成一片。孙二狗嘴张着，半天没合上，末了小声道：「……神仙。」前排一个姑娘，两只手攥在胸口。第一排的马小宝，不知不觉把腰挺得笔直。

孙二狗憋了半天，到底问出了口：「褚先生，何时我们才能像您一样，成仙，会飞啊？」褚先生从讲桌上拿起戒尺，在掌心里拍了两下，山羊胡子翘了一翘：「成仙？还早着呢。不过筑基之后，便可御剑飞行，这个倒不难。只需你们按时来听课，回去勤加练习。」满堂的眼睛都亮了。

这便是[褚先生]{注=chuxiansheng}。听说五十来岁了，看着不过三十许，脸上一条褶子也没有，只颏下一撮山羊胡子，生得精瘦，在讲经堂讲了三十年经；这一院子里，只他一个是筑了基的，旁人身上落一层灰，他那件灰袍，灰都落不上去。小满在最后一排，偷偷看了一眼自己的袖口，又看了一眼那件灰袍。踩着一口剑，从云里下来——他心里只剩一句话：这辈子，我也要这么飞上一回。

讲经堂是一间大屋，地底下压着一道细细的灵脉，砖缝里一早一晚渗出一点白气，贴着地皮流，流到前头几排，还有膝盖高，流到后头，只剩一层薄霜似的影子。前头几排坐的是真灵根，后头几排坐的是伪灵根、杂灵根，这是谁也没定过的规矩，可谁都照着坐。小满坐在最后一排，孙二狗坐在他左边，马小宝凭着荐书，坐在第一排。

褚先生背着手，摇头晃脑地讲道：「天地之间，灵气充盈。凡人不能纳，修士能纳。何也？——灵根也。一门者，天灵根；二门者，真灵根；三门者，弱灵根；四门者，伪灵根——」山羊胡子一翘，目光不偏不倚停在小满身上，「——五门俱全的，你们叫杂灵根，四面漏风。」满堂登时哄笑起来，有人拿指头在桌上敲着节拍：「漏勺！漏勺！」褚先生叫道：「沈小满。你说，漏勺能打水吗？」
story.en:
The new disciples had lessons each day at the hour of Chen. On the first day the bell had already gone and the new disciples in the lecture hall were still whispering among themselves when someone said "Huh?" and pointed out of the window. The cloud halfway up the back mountain was being parted from within: a green light came slanting down, not fast, like a leaf drifting down the wind. As it came near they saw it was a man standing on a sword, his grey robe filled out by the wind, both great sleeves streaming behind him, the hem rolling, the tuft of beard on his chin streaming too; round him wound a thin white breath, like a wisp torn from the cloud on the mountainside, travelling with him. He skimmed over three rooflines, and not one of the sparrows along the ridges took fright. The whole hall crowded to the windows, those at the back standing on the benches, Sun Ergou on tiptoe with his chin on Xiaoman's shoulder.

At the lecture-hall door the green light stopped and scattered. He stepped down off the sword, and his feet touched the ground without a sound; only then did the billowing robe slowly settle. The white breath that seeped up between the bricks, which had been flowing lazily along the ground, now surged all together toward his feet and swirled round his shoes, like a pack of dogs that has seen its master. He beckoned with two fingers, and the sword gave a soft *ting* and slid back by itself into the sheath on his back; he came in with his hands behind his back. The hall went silent all at once. The hairs on the napes of those sitting by the door stood up first, like opening a door in winter into a gust of cold — and yet it was not cold: it was all the spirit qi in the room going to him. Someone stood up first, nobody knew who, and then the whole room was standing, bench legs scraping the bricks in a long creak and squeal. Sun Ergou's mouth hung open a long while; at last he said, very quietly: "…An immortal." A girl in the front rows had both hands clasped at her breast. In the first row Ma Xiaobao, without knowing it, had sat up ramrod straight.

Sun Ergou held it in a long while, and at last it came out: "Master Chu, when will we be immortals like you, and fly?" Master Chu picked up the ruler from the lectern and tapped it twice on his palm, and his goatee twitched up. "Immortals? That's a long way off. But once you lay your Foundation you can ride a sword — that part isn't hard. Only come to your lessons on time, and go home and practise hard." Every eye in the hall lit up.

This was Master Chu. Fifty or so, they said, yet he looked barely thirty, not a wrinkle on his face, only a tuft of goat's beard on his chin; lean, and he had lectured in the Hall of Scripture for thirty years. In all that courtyard he was the only one who had reached Foundation, and where dust settled on everyone else, it would not settle on his grey robe. In the back row Xiaoman stole a look at his own cuffs, and then another at that grey robe. Standing on a sword, coming down out of the clouds — only one thought was left in him: some day in this life, I'm going to fly like that.

The Hall of Scripture was one big room with a thin spirit vein pressed beneath its floor; morning and evening a white breath seeped up between the bricks and flowed along the ground — knee-high by the front rows, and by the back no more than a frost-thin shadow. The true roots sat in front and the false and mixed roots at the back — nobody had ever made it a rule, and everybody kept it. Xiaoman sat in the back row with Sun Ergou on his left; Ma Xiaobao, on the strength of his letter, sat in the front.

Master Chu, hands behind his back, wagged his head and lectured: "Between heaven and earth, spirit qi is everywhere. Ordinary men cannot take it in; cultivators can. Why? — Spirit roots. One gate: a heavenly root; two gates: a true root; three gates: a weak root; four gates: a false root —" the goat's beard tilted up, and his eyes came to rest, neither left nor right, on Xiaoman, "— all five gates, what you lot call a mixed root." The whole hall roared, someone drumming the beat on the desk: "Skimmer! Skimmer!" Master Chu called, "Shen Xiaoman. Tell me — can a skimmer draw water?"

exits.means: answers that a skimmer can carry water — by going back more times

story.zh:
小满说：「能。」

满堂都是一愣，褚先生也愣了，山羊胡子翘在半空里，半晌才道：「……怎么打？」

小满说：「多打几次。」

满堂又笑了，只是这一回笑的方向，跟方才有点不一样：前头几排回过头来瞧他，像瞧一个说胡话的傻子；后头几排的杂灵根们却不回头，一个个低着头，肩膀一抽一抽的。小满坐下，胸口的木牌里，一个又困又不耐烦的声音在他耳朵里道：「……谁在吵？」他压低了头：「先生说杂灵根是漏勺。」那声音哼了一声：「他懂个屁。」

褚先生却不恼。这四个字，每三年开一回山门，他总要听见一回。他把戒尺在讲桌上一敲：「多打几次。好。《列子》上有个愚公，快九十岁了，嫌两座大山挡了家门，带着儿孙一筐一筐挑土。邻家的智叟笑他，他说：我死了，还有儿子；儿子又生孙子，子子孙孙没有穷尽，山却不会再长高。——后来呢？天帝感他的诚，派两个大力神，把山背走了。」他拿戒尺朝最后一排一指，「诸位记着：山，是神仙背走的。愚公挖了一辈子，挖下来几筐土？沈小满，你家里有子子孙孙替你挖么？你有神仙么？」

前头几排又笑了。小满张了张嘴。木牌里方才还骂过一句「他懂个屁」。话到了舌尖，一个「藏」字压了下去。他道：「……没有。」

褚先生道：「那就记着：漏勺，便是漏勺。坐下。」

这一回，后排没有一个人低头笑。
story.en:
"It can," said Xiaoman.

The whole hall was taken aback; so was Master Chu, his goat's beard left sticking up in mid-air. It was a while before he said, "…How?"

"Go back for more," said Xiaoman.

The hall laughed again, only this time the laughter ran a little differently: the front rows turned to look at him like a boy talking nonsense; the mixed roots in the back didn't turn, only bent their heads, shoulders twitching. Xiaoman sat down, and from the token on his chest a sleepy, impatient voice said in his ear: "…Who's making that racket?" He ducked his head. "The master says mixed roots are skimmers." The voice snorted. "What does he know."

Master Chu wasn't put out. Every three years, when the gate opened, he heard those words once. He rapped his ruler on the desk. "Draw it a few more times. Good. In the *Liezi* there's a Foolish Old Man, near ninety, who resented two great mountains blocking his door and set his sons and grandsons carrying earth away basket by basket. The Wise Elder next door laughed at him, and he said: when I die there are my sons; sons have grandsons, sons and grandsons without end, and the mountains will grow no higher. — And then? Moved by his sincerity, the Lord of Heaven sent two giants to carry the mountains away." He pointed his ruler at the back row. "Gentlemen, remember: the mountains were carried off by gods. The Old Man dug all his life — how many baskets of earth did he shift? Shen Xiaoman, have you sons and grandsons to dig for you? Have you a god?"

The front rows laughed again. Xiaoman opened his mouth. A moment ago the token had said *what does he know*. The words were on his tongue, and one word held them down: *hide*. He said, "…No."

Master Chu said, "Then remember: a skimmer is a skimmer. Sit down."

This time no one in the back rows ducked their head to laugh.
